name: UEW Ultimate Championship
notes: The fed's own top singles title throughout its attested run, 1996-1997.
epitaph: The UEW's own top singles belt, changing hands at least eight times across 1996-97 -- most memorably three separate reigns for one wrestler, ended when a challenger dethroned him with the finisher "Southern Comfort" at the fed's own Holiday Horror 2.

name: UEW American Championship
notes: The fed's own second-ranked singles title; billed the "North American Title" in 1996 before the 1997 rename.
epitaph: The UEW's own second singles belt, twice held by the same wrestler across the fed's run -- lost to a cage-match challenger at the first Holiday Horror, then reclaimed and defended in a Triple Threat at the second.

name: UEW Television Championship
notes: The fed's own third-ranked singles title.
epitaph: The UEW's own third singles belt, absorbing the retired Internet Championship in a 1997 ladder match before settling, by year's end, into the hands of the fed's own self-billed longest-reigning Television champion.

name: UEW Internet Championship
notes: Retired 15 March 1997, unified into the UEW Television Championship in a ladder match.
epitaph: A short-lived UEW singles belt with one recorded holder, retired into the Television Championship in a ladder match at the fed's own Ides of March PPV.

name: UEW Ultimate Tag Team Championship
notes: The fed's own top tag title throughout its attested run.
epitaph: The UEW's own top tag straps, held four times running by one team before a multi-team scaffold match at Holiday Horror 2 handed them to a pair of challengers on the same night the fed's Television Tag belts changed hands too.

name: UEW Television Tag Team Championship
notes: The fed's own second-ranked tag title, decided by an eight-team tournament in April 1997.
epitaph: The UEW's own second tag straps, settled by an eight-team April 1997 tournament and last seen changing hands in the same Holiday Horror 2 scaffold match that also crowned new Ultimate Tag Team Champions.

name: UEW Cruiserweight Championship
notes: Introduced as an international invitational battle royal at the fed's own 1999 New Year's supercard; billed at its introduction as the European Cruiserweight Grand Prix Invitational Championship before settling into everyday use as the Cruiserweight title.
epitaph: The UEW's newest belt, born out of a fifteen-man international battle royal and successfully defended twice inside its first three months by the man who won it.
